feature: A gap that cannot close says why
summary: Delete or Shift Delete on a gap that cannot close now puts a pill under the canvas naming what is in the way, such as Audio is locked or A caption is in the way, instead of only beeping. A clip whose own sound sits on a locked track now stays put too: before, the gap closed and the sound moved on its locked track.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default.

try.do: Open the talk sample from the Welcome window.
Click the ruler at 0:04 and press I, click at 0:08 and press O, then press semicolon to lift it.
Lock the Audio track with the lock switch in its header.
Click the gap on V1 and press Delete.
Press Shift Delete on the same gap: the same pill.
Unlock Audio, click the gap and press Delete: it closes.

evaluate: Does the pill land where your eye already is when Delete seems to do nothing?
Is Not closed, then the name of what is in the way, the right pair of words, or would the reason alone read better?
Should a locked Audio track keep the talk on V1 from sliding back, as it now does, the way a locked track holds everything on it?
Is the system beep alongside the pill welcome, or is the pill enough on its own?
rough: No mock draws a refused gap close; the pill is the existing notice under the canvas, the same one Command R uses when no clip is picked.

The right-click Ripple Delete row is dimmed when the gap cannot close, as before, but no walk photographs that menu (an open menu needs the Mac to itself); the dimming reads the same answer the pill does, and unit tests cover that answer.
Music in the way of a clip's own sound never refuses a close: the sound moves onto a free audio track instead, so in practice only a caption is ever named as in the way.
